That's breathing. That's the air filling your lungs, sharp and clear.

When you say, "I don't know," and mean it—not as a gap to be filled quickly, but as a place to stand and look around. When you let someone see you hesitate, and they don't pull back—they lean in. There was a firefly.

I was walking home late one summer night, and I'd just argued with myself—really, really argued—about something that mattered. I was angry at the world for being so loud, so careless, so full of people who were just… going through the motions. I was tired of pretending I didn't notice. And then, right there in the shadow of the old oak by the creek, it happened.

Not a metaphor. Not a "feeling." A literal, tiny pinprick of light in the black.

I stopped. I didn't even realize I'd stopped until the world went silent around me. Not quiet—*silent*. No traffic, no distant chatter, not even the wind in the leaves. Just the hum of my own pulse, and that little light, hovering just above the water. It wasn't bright enough to see clearly, but it was *there*. And it was moving—not just floating, but *choosing* its path. A little dance. A little defiance.

In that second, something in me broke open. Not shattered, but opened. Like a door that had been locked for years finally clicked.

I felt the thin air of my usual life rush out of me—a sigh that wasn't relief, but release. And in its place, I felt the real air. The air that tastes like possibility. The air that makes your throat sing when you're happy. The air that feels like a secret you're sharing with the universe.

That's when I learned the difference. Not from a book, not from a lecture. From a creature that was smaller than my hand, and yet, in that moment, it made me feel larger than myself.

It taught me that thin air is just air that hasn't been given a reason to matter yet. And that real air isn't a constant—it's an event. A happening. A collision of beauty and attention.

I've been collecting those collisions ever since.
